info.title: IOTA Hub Public API v1
info.description:
The versioned public surface of IOTA Hub, for scripts and agents: create an observation draft, upload its files, run the observer checks, fix or dismiss findings, submit — plus read access to events, observations and their files.

Authentication is the `X-API-Key` header alone. A key acts as its owner: it can never do or see more than that person can in the web app. There is no CORS on this surface, so keys stay out of browsers — call it from a script, not from a page.

The quickstart, error table and limits are at /developers.

servers.description: The environment serving this document. Until the production release, only the development deployment serves the public API, and that is where third-party developers build: sign up there, create a key, and point your client at this base URL. The production base URL is published at release.

tags.name: Public API v1
tags.description: The versioned public surface at `/public/v1`, for scripts and agents. **Authentication is the `X-API-Key` header alone** — `Authorization` and the mock-auth headers are ignored here, and there is no CORS, so keys stay out of browsers. **A key acts as its owner**: it resolves to that user's real `UserContext`, so this surface can never do or see more than the same person can in the web app, and never less on the endpoints it exposes. Least privilege comes from the surface itself — reviewer and coordinator workflow is simply not mounted here — plus the key's scopes (`observations:write` for every write, `read` for every read). The response models are frozen and additive-only within v1; every error is problem-details (`{code, message, hint, details}`) with a stable `code` to branch on, and every 429 carries `Retry-After`. Submission is collapsed for scripts: create a draft declaring its files, POST each presigned target to S3, finalize, poll the observation resource (`readiness`, `checks`, `next_actions`), then submit.

post.summary: Create a draft and presign its uploads
post.description:
Create a draft observation and, in the same call, presign one upload target per declared file. POST each file straight to S3 with the returned `upload_url` and `fields`, then call `finalize`.

Identity fields (observer, asteroid, star, time, result) are not accepted: they are read from the report spreadsheet when the `report` slot is finalized.

post.summary: Commit the declared uploads and start the checks
post.description:
Verify that every file declared at create landed in S3, commit each one onto the draft, parse the report, and make sure an observer check run is under way. Poll `GET /public/v1/observations/{id}` for the result.

A slot whose object is missing answers `409 upload_missing` with `details.slot`; the uploads that did land stay staged, so uploading the missing one and calling finalize again completes the draft.

post.description:
Start an observer check run over a draft and return it immediately with `status: running`. Poll `GET /public/v1/observations/{id}` for the findings.

Limited to 100 runs per hour **per API key**; a 429 carries `Retry-After`.

post.description:
Dismiss one finding with a written explanation, so it stops blocking submit. The note and the fact that an API key made the dismissal are carried onto the event at submit and read by the reviewer — dismissing hides nothing.

A finding of the required-items check cannot be dismissed (`422 not_dismissable`): supply the missing item instead.

post.description:
Submit the draft: match or create its event, attach, and flip it to `submitted`.

Stable codes: `422 missing_required` (`details.missing_required`), `409 open_findings` (`details.open_findings`), `409 checks_stale`, `409 already_submitted`, `409 stale_version`, `409 event_files_conflict`.

get.description:
Fetch a single observation or draft. A draft answers only to its owner — to anyone else it is a 404, so an id can never be probed for existence.

For a draft the response is self-describing: `readiness` says what is still missing, `checks` carries the latest observer-check run (null when it has never been checked), and `next_actions` gives the stable verbs to follow next.

List occultation events, newest first, with the same filters the web app offers. Results are cursor-paginated: pass the `next_cursor` from one page as `?cursor=` to get the next, and stop when it is null.

Event files are only included for callers who can see them in the UI — before an event is COMPLETE, `files` is null unless you hold `event.files.view_pre_complete`.

get.summary: Download links for an event's files
get.description:
Time-limited presigned GET URLs for the current version of every populated event file slot, plus every attachment. `slot` repeats for the multi-file slots (`damit`, `ground_track`) and is `attachment` for attachments.

Event files are private until the event is COMPLETE: before that, a caller without `event.files.view_pre_complete` gets an empty list rather than an error — the same thing the web app shows them.

List submitted observations, newest first, with the same filters the web app offers. Cursor-paginated: pass `next_cursor` as `?cursor=`.

Pass `submission_status=draft` to list **your own** drafts instead; drafts are never visible to anyone but their owner, whatever else is in the query. Observer email addresses are present only on observations you own, unless your account can see them in the UI.

get.summary: Download links for an observation's files
get.description:
Time-limited presigned GET URLs for the current version of every populated slot, plus every attachment (`slot` is `attachment` for those) and the export zip when one exists.

You can download files from your own observations; downloading someone else's needs the same permission the web app requires (`observation.view_pii`), otherwise the call is a 403.

PublicObservation.title: PublicObservation
PublicObservation.description:
An observation (draft or submitted) as the public API returns it.

Self-describing by design: a client polls this one resource and learns the
submission state, what is still missing, the latest check findings, and
the verbs to act on next (design § 7).

PublicObservationMetadata.title: PublicObservationMetadata
PublicObservationMetadata.description:
The observation's identity and result fields.

The first eight are **report-derived**: they are written from the parsed
report spreadsheet and cannot be set directly (design § 5). The last two
are observer-owned flags that change what submit requires.

state.title: State
state.description: 'in_progress' (required items missing or event files blocking), 'checking' (checks absent, running or stale), 'needs_attention' (open findings), or 'ready'.

missing_required.title: Missing Required
missing_required.description: Stable keys still absent: report, lightcurve, log, result_type, asteroid_id, asteroid_id_confirmation, asteroid_name, star, observed_at_utc, observer_name, observer_email.

open_findings.title: Open Findings
open_findings.description: Non-dismissed findings on the latest run

dismissed_findings.title: Dismissed Findings
dismissed_findings.description: Dismissed findings on the latest run

checks_current.title: Checks Current
checks_current.description: True when the latest complete run describes the draft as it stands

event_files_blocked.title: Event Files Blocked
event_files_blocked.description: Staged event files would conflict with an existing event on submit

latest_run_id.title: Latest Run Id
latest_run_id.description: Id of the latest observer check run, if any

PublicReadiness.title: PublicReadiness
PublicReadiness.description: Derived submit readiness of a draft (never stored).

code.title: Code
code.description: Stable outcome identifier: 'partial' with status 'parsed'; 'unreadable', 'version_not_detected', 'unsupported_version' or 'no_metadata' with status 'failed'.

PublicReportParse.title: PublicReportParse
PublicReportParse.description: Outcome of the server-side parse of the ``report`` slot.

version.title: Version
version.description: The version you last read. A mismatch answers 409 so a concurrent change is never submitted unseen.

filename.title: Filename

PublicUploadTarget.description:
A presigned POST target for one declared file.

Upload with a multipart POST: the ``fields`` go in the form body and the
file part comes last.

ApiKeyAuth.name: X-API-Key
ApiKeyAuth.description: Personal API key, created on your IOTA Hub profile page and shown once. Format `iotahub_<key_id>_<secret>`. Scopes are fixed at creation: `read` for every read, `observations:write` for every write.
